messages:
maya: FYI — ops+security will perform a GitHub org team rename and SSO cutover for our CI service tomorrow 2026-03-24 22:00 UTC. This will affect team membership names, a couple of repo permissions, and the SAML provider used by our self-hosted runners.

maya: TL;DR: renames (team-legacy -> infra-ci, team-build -> infra-build), update any repo-based protections that reference the old team slugs, and rotate the SAML provider for CI runners. Downtime: <5m for runner reauth; no data loss.

aj: ack — what's the exact window and rollback plan?

maya: Window 22:00–22:30 UTC. We'll do dry-run steps at 21:30 in a test org first. Rollback is re-mapping team slugs back and re-applying the previous SAML config. ops-bot will run the migration script and emit a status webhook.

devon: which repos need manual updates? any repo that has branch protection referencing the old team slug, and any GitHub Actions workflows that hardcode org/team in e.g. `uses: org/team/.github` or `with: team: team-legacy`. I listed known repos in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-4567

sarah: I have two repos (inference-serving, model-rollouts) that use team-legacy in CODEOWNERS — will the rename keep CODEOWNERS mappings intact?

security: CODEOWNERS lines are path-based; renaming a team slug changes the reference. Please update CODEOWNERS to the new `@redwood/infra-ci` or `@redwood/infra-build` before the cutover or we'll see failures on protected branches. We will patch during the maintenance window if owners aren't updated, but prefer pre-change edits.

aj: any changes needed for OAuth apps / GitHub Apps?

maya: No client_id changes. But the CI GitHub App will be re-authorized against the new SAML provider for runner sessions. If your workflow relies on user-scoped tokens that reference team membership, double-check membership after 22:05 UTC.

devon: sample commands for maintainers?

maya: Sure — to find references:
```bash
# find CODEOWNERS entries
grep -R "team-legacy" . || true
# find workflows that mention the old team
grep -R "team-legacy" .github/workflows || true
```
And to replace locally before pushing:
```bash
git checkout -b fix/codeowners-teamname
git grep -l "team-legacy" | xargs sed -i "s/team-legacy/infra-ci/g"
git commit -am "replace team-legacy -> infra-ci"
git push origin HEAD
```

maya: ops-bot will run the canonical migration script during the window: `scripts/github/rename-team-and-rotate-saml.sh --teams team-legacy:infra-ci team-build:infra-build --dry-run` then without `--dry-run`. It will post status to #eng and update the ticket.

ops-bot: @channel Starting dry-run in test org at 21:30 UTC. Live cutover scheduled for 22:00 UTC. Will post start/completion times.

aj: who should I ping if a deploy fails because of CODEOWNERS auth?

maya: Ping @devon or @sarah first; if it looks like a SAML runner reauth issue, escalate to @security and ops on-call. We'll have runbook step 4 to re-register the runner: `./scripts/runners/reconnect.sh <runner-id>`

sarah: noted. I'll open PRs to update CODEOWNERS for inference-serving and model-rollouts today.

devon: I'll scan our repos and tag as-needed in the ticket. If anyone sees unexpected 403s post-cutover, please add a short post in this thread with repo name + workflow run link.

maya: Thanks all. Post-mortem + checklist will be attached to PLAT-4567. Small ask: try not to merge large refactors into protected branches during the 21:00–23:00 UTC window. :thumbsup:

security: post-change monitoring: we'll validate team membership counts and sample a few deploys. If we detect >5% failed runner auths across builds, we'll auto-rollback the SAML change.

ops-bot: Live cutover started at 22:00:43 UTC. Applying team renames.

ops-bot: Live cutover completed at 22:02:11 UTC. SAML provider rotated. No runner reauth errors detected during verification window.

maya: closing — looks green. If you hit anything, drop details here and we'll triage.

aj: thanks — nice and smooth.

sarah: thanks folks, PRs merged and verified.

devon: done scanning, no stray references left.

maya: closing thread; final status attached to the ticket.
